text:
Kevin: quick heads up — i'm about to merge a tf refactor that moves most provider declarations into a shared `modules/providers` module. main motivation is to avoid duplicate provider blocks across cluster modules and make aliasing consistent. can folks do a quick sanity check on secrets wiring and kube provider aliases?

Tara: thanks for the ping. high-level q: are we changing provider source/version pins or just moving blocks?

Kevin: just moving blocks and hoisting aliases. not changing provider versions in this PR. i left the lockfile untouched here — plan shows no provider version changes locally.

Sophia: quick note — when you hoist kube provider aliases, watch for modules that use implicit provider inheritance. some modules pass provider = kubernetes but rely on local provider config. double-check those callsites.

Jamal: can you paste the provider snippet you moved? makes it easier to eyeball aliasing.

Kevin: sure — here is the simplified provider layout i added in modules/providers/main.tf:

```hcl
provider "kubernetes" {
  alias = "prod"
  config_path = var.kubeconfig_prod
}

provider "kubernetes" {
  alias = "staging"
  config_path = var.kubeconfig_staging
}

provider "helm" {
  alias = "prod"
}
```

Kevin: modules now reference like `provider = kubernetes.prod` where they need the prod cluster. i also added a README in that module explaining state implications and notes on `terraform init -reconfigure` if you switch the lockfile.

Tara: ok. two quick checks: 1) make sure any module that previously relied on default provider still works (no provider param passed). 2) secrets: are we moving any secret paths or k8s secret manifests?

Kevin: not moving secret paths. the tf resources that create k8s_secret remain in the same modules. only the provider block moved. i ran a local `terraform plan` in staging and it was noop for resource changes.

Sophia: sounds reasonable. one more gotcha — terragrunt or wrapper scripts that call `terraform init` with `-reconfigure` might rotate providers unexpectedly because of the lockfile location. do we have automation to regenerate root lockfiles in CI?

Jamal: we have a plan pipeline job that will run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` for changed modules, but it only triggers on provider version changes. since we didn't change versions, it won't update the lockfile. i can run a manual regenerate in the canary workspace after merge.

Kevin: thanks. can someone run a smoke `plan` in canary once i merge? i don't want surprises when the dedicated clusters pick up the new refs.

Sophia: i'll run the canary plan after you merge. FYI i'll watch for `provider reinitialization required` in the plan output.

plan-bot: triggered: terraform plan for workspace=canary-clusters by @sophia — job queued.

infra-bot: reminder: if any state move is necessary, file a follow-up that lists `terraform state mv` commands.

Tara: if plan looks clean :thumbsup: — i'll approve the PR.

Kevin: merging in ~10m. thanks all for the rapid checks.

Sophia: plan complete — no resource changes, only provider config metadata updated. no reinit warnings. LGTM.

Tara: approving now. :shipit:

Jamal: i'll do a manual lockfile regen in staging tomorrow morning to be safe.

Kevin: perfect. will open a small follow-up to remind about the `terraform init` note in ops-runbook. thanks!
